clue.text: Information source against discretion

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
tact is discretion in dealing with others

explanation.surface: Someone weighs a source of information against the need to be discreet.
explanation.definitionFit: A contact is a person you know who can pass you useful information, an informant of sorts.

clue.text: Ready for fire with source of coal in control room?

parts.note: to cock a gun is to make it ready to fire
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Getting a fire going with coal from a hearth in a control room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' looks like a first-letter signal, but 'source of coal' is a whole phrase meaning a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockpit is the compartment from which a pilot controls an aircraft.

clue.text: Some Russian music fan, crazy, entirely losing head

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fan
crackers means crazy

indicators.note: losing head drops the first letter of the word for entirely

parts.note: quite means entirely, completely

explanation.surface: A fan of Russian music goes completely mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nutcracker Suite is Tchaikovsky's orchestral suite from his ballet, so some Russian music.

clue.text: It aggravates PA out of time (one expected to take note)

indicators.note: out of says the time letter is taken away from the PA system

parts.note: Tannoy is a British trade name for a public-address (PA) system

indicators.note: expected to take puts the note letter inside the word for one

parts.note: ace is one, the single pip on a card

explanation.surface: A personal assistant who is late is irritating, being someone supposed to take notes.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is not a personal assistant but a public-address system, the Tannoy, a British brand name; drop its T.
explanation.definitionFit: An annoyance is a thing that irritates, so it aggravates.

clue.text: Repeated instances of point duty, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for duty is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: tax is a duty paid to the state

explanation.surface: A traffic officer on point duty talks of repeated episodes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacks are small sharp pins, each one a point, so several of them are repeated points.

clue.text: French are following piano in ballad — they absorb lots

indicators.note: following puts the French word after the other piece
in places the piano letter within the word for a ballad

parts.note: a ballad is a song
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
es is French for are, as in tu es

explanation.surface: A French musical note: the French are performing after a piano ballad, and they lap it all up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponges are porous things that soak up a great deal of liquid.

clue.text: Stop company taking out one line in wine

indicators.note: in places the company abbreviation inside the shortened wine
taking out removes a single line letter from the wine

parts.note: Semillon is a white wine grape
one L, the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A firm halts by withdrawing one product line of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Semillon has two Ls; 'one line' takes out just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicolon is a punctuation mark, and punctuation marks are called stops.

clue.text: A bundle picked up and taken away from detailed talk

indicators.note: taken away from removes the reversed bundle word from the word for detailed

parts.note: elaborate means detailed

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a bale is a bundle, of hay say

explanation.surface: A bundle is lifted and removed while a detailed talk goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal speech, to hold forth.

clue.text: Lack of concentration and hard work when customer with money enters

indicators.note: enters puts the three pieces inside the word for hard work

parts.note: a grind is hard tedious work
as means when
a shopper is a customer

explanation.surface: A shop worker loses focus amid a slog when a paying customer comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasshopper mind jumps from topic to topic, unable to concentrate.

clue.text: Year amongst half-hearted environmentalists brought about end to very co-ordinated action

indicators.note: amongst puts the year letter inside the reversed environmentalists
brought about means turned round, so the word reads backwards
half-hearted takes away one of the two central Es

parts.note: Greens are environmental campaigners

indicators.note: end to picks the last letter of very

explanation.surface: After a year among lukewarm environmentalists, teamwork finally appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' leaves GRENS; 'brought about' turns it to SNERG.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergy is combined working that achieves more than separate efforts, so co-ordinated action.

clue.text: Economic restriction and — what's that? — abundant supply?

parts.note: a cut is a reduction in spending
come again? is a colloquial request to repeat something

explanation.surface: Someone half-hears talk of an economic squeeze and a plentiful supply and asks for it again.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut-and-come-again describes a plentiful supply that can be helped from repeatedly, originally of food at table.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a plentiful source from which one can keep taking more, so it means abundance.

clue.text: Side that's right in the money?

indicators.note: in puts the right abbreviation inside the word for money

parts.note: pay is the money one earns
RT is an abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

explanation.surface: A question about which team is in a lucrative position.
explanation.definitionFit: A party is one side in a legal case or dispute.

clue.text: Win gold? Then who'll take it off you?

parts.note: a win is a success
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A champion wonders who will next take the gold medal away from them.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who follows you in a title or post takes it over from you, hence the playful definition.

clue.text: Inclined to geekiness? Cachet nil, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A geek's lack of social prestige is lamented.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone technical is drawn to machines and know-how, which is what a geek is drawn to.

clue.text: Club regular brought in whip for soft cheese

indicators.note: brought in puts the club regular inside the whip

parts.note: the cat, cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
a member belongs to a club

explanation.surface: A clubgoer is lashed into bringing the cheese course.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft, creamy French cheese from Normandy.

clue.text: Barrack totally emptied in pillage

parts.note: to barrack is to jeer, to boo

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside of the word totally, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Soldiers' quarters stripped bare during a looting spree.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillage as a noun is plunder, the goods seized by force.

clue.text: Male collared by sponsor wanting reduction in theatre area

indicators.note: collared by puts the male inside the shortened sponsor word
wanting reduction cuts the last letter off the sponsor word

parts.note: a backer is a sponsor
a stag is a male deer, or a man at a men-only party

explanation.surface: A man is grabbed by a sponsor wanting a discount for theatre tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage is the area behind the stage, out of the audience's view.

clue.text: Daughter is leaving unconnected island

indicators.note: leaving says the daughter letter and the word is depart from the longer word

parts.note: discrete means separate, unconnected

explanation.surface: A daughter walks out, cut off from her family, on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the large Greek island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Windies music plays freely after start of crucial over

indicators.note: after puts the anagram behind the first letter
start of picks the first letter of crucial
freely lets the letters of plays move about

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A West Indies cricketer bats freely once a crucial over has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: Windies is the West Indies cricket team; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a style of Caribbean song originating in Trinidad.

clue.text: Regarding city affairs, European city reduced independence, linking to China

indicators.note: reduced cuts the last letter from the name of the city

parts.note: Munich is the Bavarian city
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent
china is cockney rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, a pal

explanation.surface: A city's municipal affairs: a German city loses autonomy while forging ties with China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: in rhyming slang china plate means mate, so PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal means relating to a town or city and its local government.

clue.text: Blue clothing? Nothing racy in this!

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling low
gear is clothing

explanation.surface: Racy blue clothing turns out to be nothing of the sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racy' seems to mean risqué, picking up 'Blue', but it means fast: you cannot race in low gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle in its lowest gear moves slowly, so no speed is possible in it.

clue.text: Chopped sausage found in toilets in US city

indicators.note: found in puts the shortened sausage inside the word for toilets

parts.note: loos is British slang for toilets

indicators.note: chopped cuts the end off the sausage word

parts.note: salami is a sausage

explanation.surface: Bits of sausage discovered in public toilets in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' looks like an anagram signal but just cuts off the last letter, leaving SALAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Alamos is the New Mexico town where the atomic bomb was developed.

clue.text: Free round got in by miss

indicators.note: got in by puts the round letter inside the word for miss

parts.note: to lose is to miss, as a chance
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A free round of drinks bought by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means free, unconfined.

clue.text: Strikes? Tons lost from investments

indicators.note: lost from takes the ton letter out of the investments

parts.note: stocks are investments

explanation.surface: Industrial action leads to heavy losses on the stock market.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is to hit them hard, so socks are blows.

clue.text: Second growth turned over for fodder

indicators.note: turned over says the word for a growth is written backwards

parts.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: A farmer's second crop is ploughed in to feed livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried stalks of cereal are used as bedding and as coarse feed for animals.

clue.text: Threatening item is concealed, I hope (no end of trouble if let loose)

indicators.note: let loose frees the letters to rearrange themselves
no takes the final letter of trouble away from the word hope
end of picks the final letter of trouble

explanation.surface: A threatening object is hidden away, with the hope that releasing it will cause no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of trouble' removes E (the last letter of trouble) from HOPE, leaving HOP; 'let loose' then shuffles IS CONCEALED I HOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoned chalice is an apparent prize that will harm whoever takes it, so a menacing thing.

clue.text: Each is engaged in public stuff

indicators.note: is engaged in puts the abbreviation for each inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, public

explanation.surface: Every one of them is busy with the public's business.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to eat too much, a verb sense.

clue.text: Graceful line penned by one initiating correspondence

indicators.note: penned by puts the line letter inside the word for a letter-writer

parts.note: a sender starts an exchange of letters

explanation.surface: A letter-writer pens an elegant line to start a correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slim and elegant in shape, hence graceful.
